title: Images and Alt Text
summary: Add images with src and meaningful alt text.

sketchBlocks.title: An image needs src and meaningful alt text
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown: The `` element embeds an image. `src` tells the browser where the image file is, and `alt` provides a text alternative. ```html ``` This line has two jobs: the source path tells the browser which file to load, while the alternative text communicates the picture's meaningful content when the image cannot be seen. `` is a void element, so it does not wrap content with a separate closing tag.

sketchBlocks.title: Alt text should communicate the image's purpose
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown: Useful alt text explains information that matters in context. ```html ``` This line pairs the image file with a concise description of what matters in the scene. Avoid alternatives such as `image`, `photo`, or a raw filename; a learner who cannot see the picture should still understand why it is present.

sketchBlocks.title: Image paths follow the same path rules
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown: The `src` attribute follows the same path rules used by link destinations. ```html ``` Line by line: **First**, `avatar.png` means the image is in the same folder as the current HTML document. **Second**, `media/avatar.png` means the browser must enter the `media` child folder before loading the file. The alt text can stay the same because both examples describe the same picture while demonstrating two different file locations.

quizDraft.title: Choose the image source attribute
quizDraft.prompt: Which attribute tells an img element where to find the image file?
quizDraft.hint: Think about which image attribute points to the file location.

help.concept: An image separates its file location from its text alternative.
help.hint_1: Look for the attribute that stores the path to the file.
help.hint_2: Eliminate choices used for links, text alternatives, or identifiers.

quizDraft.title: Choose useful alt text
quizDraft.prompt: Which alt value is most useful for a profile portrait?
quizDraft.hint: Describe the meaningful content instead of the file type or filename.

help.concept: Alt text should communicate what matters about the image.
help.hint_1: Avoid generic words like image or photo.
help.hint_2: Choose the description a person could understand without seeing the image.

options: Student smiling in front of the campus library

quizDraft.title: Recognize a complete image element
quizDraft.prompt: Which statements about img are correct? Choose all that apply.
quizDraft.hint: Think about image location, alternative text, and void elements.

help.concept: img uses src and alt and is a void element.
help.hint_1: Relative paths work in src just as they do in href.
help.hint_2: There is no required closing </img> tag.

options: A relative src can point into an images folder.

quizDraft.title: Assemble an image element
quizDraft.prompt: Arrange the pieces into one img element with src first and alt second.
quizDraft.hint: Start the img tag, add its attributes, then close the tag.

help.concept: Attributes belong inside the opening img tag.
help.hint_1: src and alt both appear before >.
help.hint_2: The result does not need a separate closing element.

quizDraft.title: Complete the image path
quizDraft.prompt: Choose the src value for `profile.jpg` inside the `images` folder.
quizDraft.hint: Build the value from the child folder name and the image filename.

help.concept: A relative image path can enter a child folder before naming the file.
help.hint_1: Join the folder and filename with one slash.
help.hint_2: The finished value should describe one child-folder step followed by the target file.

quizDraft.title: Complete meaningful alt text
quizDraft.prompt: Choose the most descriptive alt value.
quizDraft.hint: Describe the meaningful content of the picture.

help.concept: Alt text is a text alternative, not a filename label.
help.hint_1: Choose a concise description of what the image communicates.
help.hint_2: Avoid generic words like image or picture.

choices: Students presenting a science club poster
quizDraft.correctValue: Students presenting a science club poster

quizDraft.title: Use the supplied profile image
quizDraft.prompt: Open the `images` folder in Explorer and confirm `profile.png` is supplied. In `index.html`, add that image below the h1 and give it useful alternative text for a student profile illustration. Check the real asset in Preview.
quizDraft.hint: The image lives in a child folder of the home page.

help.concept: The image source path and alternative text work together: one locates the asset and the other communicates its purpose.
help.hint_1: Use the folder tree to build the source path.
help.hint_2: Describe the profile illustration instead of using a generic word such as image.

quizDraft.title: Improve the profile image alt text
quizDraft.prompt: The image already appears in Preview, but its alternative text is too generic. Improve the `alt` value so it identifies Jordan and describes the campus-library scene.

quizDraft.title: Make the profile image open About
quizDraft.prompt: The website includes `about.html`. Wrap the existing profile image in an anchor so clicking the image in Preview opens the About page. Keep the image source and alternative text unchanged.
quizDraft.hint: The anchor should contain the existing img element.

help.concept: Images can be interactive link content when an anchor wraps the image element.
help.hint_1: Do not replace or edit the supplied image asset.
help.hint_2: Use the neighboring About page as the anchor destination.
